title: Reachability after encoding the input symbol
statement: Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input and work-tape symbols. Let $y,x$ be finite bit strings, let $\sigma$ be a verifier state, let $R$ be a register assignment whose 21 values are all at most $B=(8W_N+8)(|y|+1)$, and let $p$ be a natural number. Write $\iota(x,p)$ for the input symbol at position $p$, taking the value “blank” when $p$ is either boundary position and otherwise the bit of $x$ at index $p-1$ (defaulting to $0$ if that index is beyond $x$). Encode these three possibilities by $0$ for blank, $1$ for false, and $2$ for true. If register $Z$ equals this code, then for some $z\le 2$ the codec program in step mode can reach the phase that starts processing the symbol $\iota(x,p)$, changing only register $Z$ to $z$ and keeping every register at most $B$ throughout the run.
hypotheses_covered: $N$ is a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over Boolean symbols
Every register value in $R$ is at most $(8W_N+8)(|y|+1)$
Register $Z$ equals the code of the input symbol at position $p$
caveat: The program phase and reachability relation are defined by a lengthy codec program. The prose summarizes their role; the formal statement does not require the extra condition $z$ to equal the symbol code.
